02 The woods

We roast the way
the woods smell.

Piney Woods Roasters started in 2018 with one drum roaster, a borrowed corner of a barn, and a stubborn idea: coffee this good shouldn't require a plane ticket to Honduras to find. So we brought the beans here.

Organic arabica from small farms in Honduras and Mexico, roasted in small batches with a hand on the drum and a nose on the exhaust. No warehouse, no year-old inventory — just coffee that still smells like the week it was made.

03 The ritual

One good cup,
three moves.

No lab coat required. This works for a pourover, a drip machine, or a dented cowboy pot over a fire.

  1. 01

    Weigh it out

    18 grams of coffee, ground medium-fine. A scoop is fine. Fresh-ground beats everything else you can do to a bag.

  2. 02

    Bloom, then pour

    Just off the boil — 94°C. Wet the grounds, wait forty seconds, then pour the rest in slow circles until you hit 300 grams.

  3. 03

    Let it finish

    Around three and a half minutes, total. Drink the first cup black. Then decide what it needs — most bags need nothing.

04 On the road

Good coffee
travels light.

Jack's Roast brew bags are pre-measured single serves: one bag, one cup, no grinder, no scale, no sad hotel-lobby coffee. Toss a handful in a carry-on, a tackle box, or the glovebox and you're covered until you get home.
